To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we mapped quantitative trait locis (QTL) for aristolochic-acid-induced nephropathy in an F2 cross of C57BL/6 J x DBA/2 J.

1) we identified a single main QTL on chromosome 4 and three interacting QTLs on chromosomes 2, 3 and 11, and 2) the Aanq1 QTL was also detected in mice that were not treated with AA, raising the possibility for preexisting differences in tubular function that may affect the severity and/or progression of AAN.

we identified genetic loci in the mouse that are associated with sensitivity to aristolochic acids and that these genetic loci may contribute to human susceptibility to AA-induced kidney disease and cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying genetic factors contributing to the development of aristolochic-acid-induced kidney injury in mice and humans.
the identification of genes that influence the sensitivity of proximal tubule cells to aristolochic acids and the elucidation of the pathways involved.
understanding the genetic basis of susceptibility to aristolochic acids in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has identified a single main QTL and three additional interacting QTLs that affect proximal tubule toxicity in mice after aristolochic acids treatment.
this study identified a single main QTL (Aanq-1), on chromosome 4 and three interacting QTLs (Aanq 2-4) on chromosomes 2, 4 and 5.
this study has identified genetic loci that affect AA-induced nephrotoxity in the mouse, which will further our understanding human susceptibility to AA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified genetic regions that affect the severity of aristolochic-acid nephrotoxicosis in the mouse.
we have identified genetic loci in mice that are associated with susceptibility to aristolochic-acid induced nephrotoxicosis.
we identified genetic loci that affect AA-induced nephrotoxity in the mouse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic loci that affect AA-induced nephrotoxicty in the mouse can be used to identify genes that affect AA-induced kidney injury in human.

there are genetic factors that influence susceptibility to AA-induced renal injury in the mouse and that this genetic susceptibility is detectable even in the absence of AA exposure, suggesting that there are pre-existing differences in proximal renal function between the strains.
genetic predisposition to AAN is a reality and that the mouse model is an excellent system in which to study the genetic basis of AAN.
